priorIterationResolution.priorFinding: FIND-011 (iteration-6, simultaneous multi-clip disambiguation math mathematically broken)
priorIterationResolution.note: REQ-008 step 2 REV 7 (behavioral-spec.md lines 165-178) eliminates the multi-clip disambiguation problem entirely rather than patching it: only the OLDEST pending clip is ever attempted in a given wake, and no other pending clip's before-set is read or diffed in that wake. Hand-traced with 2 pending clips: because clip2 is never touched while clip1 is being resolved, there is no cross-clip attribution step for the algorithm to get wrong -- the class of bug iteration-6 found (a per-clip diff against an independently-captured before-set being confused by another clip's own legitimate new post) cannot occur, since there is only ever one clip's before-set in play per wake. The remaining, narrower collision (this ONE clip's own diff vs. the SAME wake's independent new-content pipeline) is a genuinely different, smaller-surface-area problem, explicitly acknowledged and handled as 'ambiguous -> inconclusive, never guess' (REQ-008 step 6). This is a real simplification, not a re-patch of the broken algorithm.

REQ-008 step 2 (behavioral-spec.md lines 172-174) now specifies a concrete, existing signal: `os.path.getmtime()` on the sidecar file `<clipname>.before-hrefs.json`, justified by the sidecar already being written at the exact moment the clip enters `$CLIP_PENDING_VERIFY` (REQ-006/008 step 6) -- no new field, no new write path, no new failure mode introduced by the ordering mechanism itself.
